subject_offered_enrollment_rank.name: subject_offered_enrollment_rank
subject_offered_enrollment_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY,
  subject_offered.TERM_CODE,
  subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID,
  subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY subject_offered.TERM_CODE ORDER BY COALESCE(subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,0) DESC) AS enrollment_rank
FROM subject_offered

params.description: Ranks subjects within each term by number of enrolled students, returning one row per subject_offered summary with its term, id, title, enrolled count, and enrollment rank.
params.when_to_use: Find the most- or least-enrolled subjects in a specific term (top-N / bottom-N by enrollment). | Annotate subject_offered rows with their position (rank) in enrollment within the same term for reporting or filtering (e.g., top 10 subjects this term). | Compose into higher-level queries that need a stable per-subject-offering enrollment rank (e.g., join to subject metadata or faculty and then filter where enrollment_rank <= N).
params.output_schema: subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY: surrogate key identifying the subject_offered summary row; sourced directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY. | subject_offered.TERM_CODE: academic term code for the offered subject; sourced directly from subject_offered.TERM_CODE. Used as the RANK() partition key. | subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID: subject identifier (e.g., course/subject code) for the offered subject; sourced directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID. | subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE: descriptive title of the subject offering; sourced directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE. | subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS: count of enrolled students for this subject_offered summary; sourced directly from subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS and used to compute the rank (NULL treated as 0 via COALESCE in ordering). | enrollment_rank: integer rank within term (1 = highest enrollment) computed as RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY term_code ORDER BY COALESCE(num_enrolled_students,0) DESC). Ties receive the same rank and leave gaps according to RANK semantics.
params.metric: enrollment_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY subject_offered.TERM_CODE ORDER BY COALESCE(subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, 0) DESC) | NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS = base column subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS (used as the ordering metric; NULLs treated as 0 for ranking)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to subject_offered_core on subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY = subject_offered_core.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY — safe because this view is one-row-per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY, so joining to a one-row-per-same-key source preserves cardinality and does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to subject_summary_core on subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID = subject_summary_core.SUBJECT_ID (and optionally TERM_CODE = subject_summary_core.TERM_CODE if that view is term-scoped) — safe if subject_summary_core is one-row-per subject_id (or per subject_id+term) so the subject_offered measures are not multiplied. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many children (e.g., a raw enrollments table, sections, or faculty assignments) without re-aggregation because those joins can duplicate NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS and invalidate enrollment_rank. If you must bring one-to-many detail in, either: |   - aggregate the child to one row per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY first (e.g., SUM or COUNT) and then join, or |   - join and then re-aggregate the joined result back to subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY, recalculating measures/metrics you need. | If composing further ranking or window functions partitioned by TERM_CODE, use this view's enrollment_rank as a stable input but be mindful that re-partitioning or re-aggregation may change rank semantics (e.g., RANK() vs DENSE_RANK()). | When joining to subject_offered_with_faculty (a JOIN sibling), ensure the join keys produce at most one row per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY on the right side; if subject_offered_with_faculty contains multiple faculty rows per subject_offered summary, aggregate faculty (e.g., STRING_AGG or choose a primary faculty) before joining to avoid duplicating enrollment counts and altering ranks.

subject_offered_enrollment_rank.description: Per TERM_CODE ranking of subject_offered by NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS with an explicit rank column. Use this to pick top-k subjects per term by filtering on rank. | Use for: Find top-enrolled subjects per term; Investigate enrollment distribution across terms; Select top-k rows per TERM_CODE for downstream joins

subject_summary_core.name: subject_summary_core
subject_summary_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY,
  subject_summary.TERM_CODE,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS,
  subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS,
  subject_summary.LAB_UNITS,
  subject_summary.PREP_UNITS,
  subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER,
  subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN,
  subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM subject_summary

params.description: One-row-per-subject-summary: aggregated subject-level enrollments, units, and identifiers for a term (subject_summary rows).
params.when_to_use: Report subject-level enrollment and unit totals for a given term (e.g., total students in a subject, first-week vs fifth-week enrollment). | Build dashboards that list subjects with their units and enrollment metrics (sorting, filtering by term, master subject grouping). | Compose higher-level aggregates (e.g., college or department totals) by further aggregating this view's enrollment/units. | Join subject-level attributes (title, ids, sort keys) to other datasets while preserving aggregated enrollment measures if join is 1:1.
params.output_schema: subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY: surrogate primary key for the subject_summary row (grain). Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_summary.TERM_CODE: academic term identifier for the summary row. Source column: subject_summary.TERM_CODE | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID: subject code (e.g., MATH). Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT: sort key for subject id ordering. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE: human-readable subject title. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID: master/normalized subject identifier used for grouping variants. Source column: subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT: sort key for master subject ordering. Source column: subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS: total units associated with the subject summary (aggregated units measure). Source column: subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS | subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS: units attributable to lecture component. Source column: subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS | subject_summary.LAB_UNITS: units attributable to lab component. Source column: subject_summary.LAB_UNITS | subject_summary.PREP_UNITS: units attributable to preparation component. Source column: subject_summary.PREP_UNITS | subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS: units attributable to design component. Source column: subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER: numeric count of enrolled students in the subject (aggregate at this row's grain). Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER: enrollment count for the subject cluster (if clustering applied). Source column: subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK: enrollment count measured in first week. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK: enrollment count measured in fifth week. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT: count of credit enrollments. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN: count of 'listen' (audit/non-credit) enrollments. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN | subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE: ETL load date for the row. Source column: subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.grounded_columns: subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_summary.TERM_CODE | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS | subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS | subject_summary.LAB_UNITS | subject_summary.PREP_UNITS | subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN | subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.metric: TOTAL_UNITS = subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS  -- stored aggregate (units) at the subject_summary grain | LECTURE_UNITS = subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS  -- stored units for lecture portion | LAB_UNITS = subject_summary.LAB_UNITS  -- stored units for lab portion | PREP_UNITS = subject_summary.PREP_UNITS  -- stored units for prep portion | DESIGN_UNITS = subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS  -- stored units for design portion | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER  -- stored aggregate count of enrolled students | CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER = subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER  -- stored cluster-level enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK  -- stored first-week enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK  -- stored fifth-week enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT  -- stored credit enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN  -- stored listen/audit enrollment count
params.composition: Cardinality-safe joins (do NOT duplicate measures): |  - Join to dimension-like, one-row-per-key tables/views on matching keys (example): join to a term dimension on TERM_CODE, or to a subject dimension on SUBJECT_ID or MASTER_SUBJECT_ID — safe because subject_summary is one-row-per SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY (one-row-per subject_summary) so joining 1:1 preserves measures. |  - Join to subject_offered_core on SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY (if subject_offered_core is one-row-per-SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY) — safe only if that sibling view is known to be 1:1 with subject_summary; verify sibling grain before joining. |  | Do NOT join (without re-aggregation) to known one-to-many tables/views because they will multiply this view's measures: |  - Do NOT directly join to subject_offered_with_faculty (JOIN) if that view contains one row per offering or per faculty assignment (one-to-many to subject_summary) unless you first aggregate the many-side back to subject_summary grain. Joining without re-aggregation will over-count SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_* and UNIT measures. |  - Do NOT join to subject_offered_enrollment_rank (RANK) if it is one-row-per-offering/rank (one-to-many) without reducing it to the subject_summary grain first. If you need per-offering details, compute offering-level metrics separately and avoid summing subject_summary metrics with those rows. |  | Guidance for safe composition by planners: |  - If you need to combine subject_summary metrics with a one-to-many sibling, perform an aggregated subquery on the many-side grouped to SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY before joining, e.g.: SELECT s.*, m.some_agg FROM subject_summary s LEFT JOIN (SELECT SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY, SUM(x) AS some_agg FROM many_table GROUP BY SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY) m USING (SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY). This preserves the one-row-per-subject_summary property. |  - When computing higher-level aggregates (e.g., totals by MASTER_SUBJECT_ID or TERM_CODE), aggregate the subject_summary measures (SUM(TOTAL_UNITS), SUM(SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER), etc.) grouped by the desired key — do not rely on joins to expand rows and then SUM without DISTINCT control. |  - Treat SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY as the canonical grain key for row-level uniqueness. Any join that is many-to-one into subject_summary (many rows on the other side per SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY) must be pre-aggregated back to SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY to avoid duplication.

subject_summary_core.description: Aggregated subject_summary metrics per TERM_CODE and SUBJECT_ID including enrollment snapshots and unit totals. Use for term-level subject analytics and to compare enrollment snapshots. | Use for: Compare first-week vs fifth-week enrollment; Aggregate units and enrollment metrics by subject/term; Join to department or course catalogs for reporting

SELECT

params.description: Provides one-row-per-subject_offered summary including the responsible faculty identifiers and their directory details (if available).
params.when_to_use: Look up the responsible faculty contact info for a specific subject offering (by SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY, TERM_CODE, or SUBJECT_ID). | Build reports that display subject offerings alongside faculty name, email, office and phone when each subject_offered row should stay at the subject_offered grain. | Compose further SQL that filters or aggregates subject_offered-level measures while also showing faculty attributes (safe when not introducing one-to-many expansions).
params.output_schema: subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY: unique key for this subject_offered row — derived directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_offered.TERM_CODE: term code for the subject offering — derived directly from subject_offered.TERM_CODE | subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID: subject identifier (e.g., subject code) — derived directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID | subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE: title of the subject offered — derived directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID: MIT ID of the responsible faculty for the subject offering — derived directly from subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME: responsible faculty name as stored on the subject_offered row — derived directly from subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME | employee_directory.MIT_ID: MIT ID from employee_directory (may be NULL if no matching directory row) — derived directly from employee_directory.MIT_ID | employee_directory.LAST_NAME: last name from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.LAST_NAME | employee_directory.FIRST_NAME: first name from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.FIRST_NAME | employee_directory.FULL_NAME: full name from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.FULL_NAME | employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION: office location from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION | employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE: office phone from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE | employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS: email address from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS
params.grounded_columns: subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_offered.TERM_CODE | subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID | subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME | employee_directory.MIT_ID | employee_directory.LAST_NAME | employee_directory.FIRST_NAME | employee_directory.FULL_NAME | employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION | employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE | employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS
params.metric: This view does not define any aggregated metrics. All outputs are directly selected base columns (no aggregates). If you need counts or sums, compute them by aggregating subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY (one row per key) after applying any additional joins/filters.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional lookups that are one-to-one with subject_offered keys — safe because this view is one row per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY so measures at that grain are not duplicated. | Safe to join on subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY to: subject_offered_core (SEL) — safe because subject_offered_core is a same-grain selection/view over subject_offered (one row per SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY). | Safe to join on SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY to other one-row-per-subject_offered views (for example, subject_summary_core) provided they are defined at the same SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY grain. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables or views (for example: enrollments, meeting times, student lists, or any view that aggregates at a lower-grain such as per-student or per-meeting) without re-aggregation because such joins will multiply subject_offered rows and thereby duplicate any derived counts or measures. If you need to combine with a one-to-many relationship, first aggregate the many-side to one row per SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY (for example: COUNT(*) AS enrollment_count FROM enrollment GROUP BY SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY) and then join on SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY. | If joining to employee_directory variants: this view already left-joins employee_directory by MIT_ID = subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID. Re-joining to employee_directory on the same MIT_ID is redundant. If you need additional employee attributes that exist in another employee view keyed by MIT_ID and guaranteed one-row-per-MIT_ID, you can inner-join on RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = other_employee.MIT_ID safely (one-to-one). | If you must join to subject_offered_enrollment_rank (RANK) which is likely one-row-per-subject_offered (ranked metric): verify it is one-row-per SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY before joining directly; if it is per-subject_offered then join on SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY is safe. If it is one-to-many, aggregate first.

subjects_enrollable_by_department.name: subjects_enrollable_by_department
subjects_enrollable_by_department.body_sql:
SELECT
  se.TERM_CODE                                  AS TERM_CODE,
  se.SUBJECT_ID                                 AS SUBJECT_ID,
  se.OFFER_DEPT_CODE                            AS OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  se.OFFER_SCHOOL_CODE                          AS OFFER_SCHOOL_CODE,
  so.OFFER_DEPT_NAME                            AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
  ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME                            AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  ss.SCHOOL_NAME                                AS SCHOOL_NAME,
  so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID                          AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
FROM subject_enrollable AS se
LEFT JOIN subject_offered AS so
  ON se.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
  AND se.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN subject_summary AS ss
  ON se.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE
  AND se.SUBJECT_ID = ss.SUBJECT_ID
subjects_enrollable_by_department.description: One row per subject offering (term/subject) from subject_enrollable and related subject summary/offered tables that exposes subject identifiers and department/offer department fields to allow filtering by department name/code (i.e., to find subjects students from a given department/school can enroll in).

SELECT

room_to_building_mapping.name: room_to_building_mapping
room_to_building_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT
  `fac_rooms`.`FAC_ROOM_KEY` AS `FAC_ROOM_KEY`,
  `fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  `fac_rooms`.`ROOM` AS `ROOM`,
  `fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY_2`,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY_FROM_BUILDINGS`,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_NAME` AS `BUILDING_NAME`,
  `fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_ROOM_KEY` AS `FCLT_ROOM_KEY`,
  `fclt_rooms`.`BUILDING_ROOM` AS `BUILDING_ROOM`,
  `fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_BUILDING_KEY` AS `FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`
FROM `fac_rooms`
LEFT JOIN `buildings`
  ON `fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY` = `buildings`.`BUILDING_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `fclt_rooms`
  ON (
       -- try direct match: fac_rooms building+room to fclt_rooms BUILDING_ROOM
       `fclt_rooms`.`BUILDING_ROOM` = CONCAT(
         COALESCE(`fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY`, ''), '-', COALESCE(`fac_rooms`.`ROOM`, '')
       )
       -- fallback: also allow matching just on room code if BUILDING_ROOM stores only room codes
       OR `fclt_rooms`.`BUILDING_ROOM` = `fac_rooms`.`ROOM`
       -- fallback: or match by facility building key stored in fac_rooms to fclt_rooms building key
       OR `fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_BUILDING_KEY` = `fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY`
     )
WHERE
  -- only include mappings that have at least one source identifier present
  ( (`fac_rooms`.`FAC_ROOM_KEY` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_rooms`.`FAC_ROOM_KEY` <> '')
    OR (`fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_ROOM_KEY` IS NOT NULL AND `fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_ROOM_KEY` <> '') )
room_to_building_mapping.description: Canonical mapping of room identifiers (building-room codes and meet_place values that represent rooms) to facility building keys and building names. iap_subject_detail_cleaned.name: iap_subject_detail_cleaned
iap_subject_detail_cleaned.body_sql:
SELECT
  `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY` AS IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY,
  `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` AS IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY,
  `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY` AS IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY,
  `iap_subject_detail`.`ACTIVITY_TITLE` AS ACTIVITY_TITLE,
  -- cleaned numeric ATTENDANCE: try to cast to signed, null if empty or non-numeric
  (CASE
    WHEN `iap_subject_detail`.`ATTENDANCE` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(`iap_subject_detail`.`ATTENDANCE`) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN `iap_subject_detail`.`ATTENDANCE` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(`iap_subject_detail`.`ATTENDANCE` AS SIGNED)
    WHEN `iap_subject_detail`.`ATTENDANCE` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(FLOOR(CAST(`iap_subject_detail`.`ATTENDANCE` AS DECIMAL(18,6))) AS SIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END) AS ATTENDANCE,
  -- cleaned numeric FEE: remove common non-numeric characters then cast to decimal, null if not convertible
  (CASE
    WHEN `iap_subject_detail`.`FEE` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(`iap_subject_detail`.`FEE`) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE
      (CASE
        WHEN REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(TRIM(`iap_subject_detail`.`FEE`), ',', ''), '$', ''), 'USD', '') REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$'
          THEN CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(TRIM(`iap_subject_detail`.`FEE`), ',', ''), '$', ''), 'USD', '') AS DECIMAL(18,2))
        ELSE NULL
      END)
  END) AS FEE
FROM `iap_subject_detail`
iap_subject_detail_cleaned.description: One row per iap_subject_detail offering, with cleaned numeric conversions for ATTENDANCE and FEE and preserved keys to join to sponsor and session.

  -- keep original misspelled column name if present on source table
  scd.GRADAUTE_LEVEL AS GRADAUTE_LEVEL,
  -- source timestamp for chosen GRADUATE_LEVEL (WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE from row that supplied it)
  x.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM
  -- base table with course description columns required
  sis_course_description scd
  -- for each COURSE, find the most recent non-null GRADUATE_LEVEL row (by WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE)
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      COURSE,
      GRADUATE_LEVEL,
      WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
    FROM (
      SELECT
        COURSE,
        GRADUATE_LEVEL,
        WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
          PARTITION BY COURSE
          ORDER BY
            -- prefer non-null GRADUATE_LEVEL first, then latest WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
            (GRADUATE_LEVEL IS NOT NULL) DESC,
            -- assume WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE is comparable as string timestamp; if not, clients should pass parsed values
            WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE DESC
        ) AS rn
      FROM sis_course_description
    ) t
    WHERE rn = 1
  ) x
    ON x.COURSE = scd.COURSE
course_description_graduate_level_dedup.description: Normalized course description rows with graduate-level info deduplicated to the most recent non-null GRADUATE_LEVEL per COURSE key (COURSE or CIP_PROGRAM_CODE). Provides one row per COURSE key with chosen graduate level and source timestamp to join back to schools.

tip_material_split_authors.name: tip_material_split_authors
tip_material_split_authors.body_sql:
SELECT
  tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY AS TIP_MATERIAL_KEY,
  TRIM(author_part) AS AUTHOR
FROM tip_material tm
JOIN (
  -- split AUTHORS by semicolon into rows
  SELECT
    TIP_MATERIAL_KEY,
    TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(AUTHOR, ';', seq.n), ';', -1)) AS author_part
  FROM tip_material
  JOIN (
    -- sequence numbers 1..20 (adjust max parts if needed)
    SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
    UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10
    UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15
    UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19 UNION ALL SELECT 20
  ) seq
  ON seq.n <= 1 + LENGTH(AUTHOR) - LENGTH(REPLACE(AUTHOR, ';', ''))
  WHERE AUTHOR IS NOT NULL AND AUTHOR <> ''
) split ON split.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
WHERE TRIM(split.author_part) <> ''
tip_material_split_authors.description: Normalize tip_material rows by splitting the AUTHOR field on semicolons into one row per author and trimming whitespace; exclude empty/null authors.

term_master_catalog.name: term_master_catalog
term_master_catalog.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(at.`TERM_CODE`, ata.`TERM_CODE`, atp.`TERM_CODE`) AS TERM_CODE,
  -- prefer TERM_DESCRIPTION from academic_terms, fall back to academic_terms_all, then academic_term_parameter
  COALESCE(at.`TERM_DESCRIPTION`, ata.`TERM_DESCRIPTION`, atp.`TERM_DESCRIPTION`) AS TERM_DESCRIPTION,
  -- prefer IS_CURRENT_TERM from academic_terms, fall back to academic_terms_all, then academic_term_parameter
  COALESCE(at.`IS_CURRENT_TERM`, ata.`IS_CURRENT_TERM`, atp.`IS_CURRENT_TERM`) AS IS_CURRENT_TERM
FROM
  (
    -- derive the full set of TERM_CODE values from union of term-bearing tables
    SELECT `TERM_CODE` FROM `academic_terms`
    UNION
    SELECT `TERM_CODE` FROM `academic_terms_all`
    UNION
    SELECT `TERM_CODE` FROM `academic_term_parameter`
  ) AS term_codes
LEFT JOIN `academic_terms` AS at
  ON term_codes.`TERM_CODE` = at.`TERM_CODE`
LEFT JOIN `academic_terms_all` AS ata
  ON term_codes.`TERM_CODE` = ata.`TERM_CODE`
LEFT JOIN `academic_term_parameter` AS atp
  ON term_codes.`TERM_CODE` = atp.`TERM_CODE`
term_master_catalog.description: Canonical term rows with description and current-term flag, preferring academic_terms then falling back to academic_terms_all. One row per TERM_CODE present in the union of term-bearing tables.

instructor_subject_types_history.body_sql:
SELECT

  so.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY,
  so.HGN_CODE AS HGN_CODE,
  so.CLUSTER_TYPE AS CLUSTER_TYPE,
  -- SUBJECT_OR_CLUSTER is not a stored column in the base tables; derive from CLUSTER_TYPE presence:
  -- but requirement forbids re-deriving a stored value if it exists. Because no exact source table/column SUBJECT_OR_CLUSTER is present,
  -- expose NULL so the view remains joinable and does not substitute another column.
  NULL AS SUBJECT_OR_CLUSTER,
  ccc.FALL_INSTRUCTORS AS FALL_INSTRUCTORS,
  cso.FALL_INSTRUCTORS AS COURSE_CATALOG_FALL_INSTRUCTORS,
  dcc.FALL_INSTRUCTORS AS DRUPAL_FALL_INSTRUCTORS
FROM
  subject_offered_core AS so
LEFT JOIN
  cis_course_catalog AS ccc
    ON ccc.SUBJECT_ID = so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
    AND ccc.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
LEFT JOIN
  course_catalog_subject_offered AS cso
    ON cso.SECTION_ID = so.SECTION_ID
    AND cso.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
LEFT JOIN
  drupal_course_catalog AS dcc
    ON dcc.SECTION_ID = so.SECTION_ID
    AND dcc.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
WHERE
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME IS NOT NULL

instructor_course_offerings.name: instructor_course_offerings
instructor_course_offerings.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY,
  so.TERM_CODE                                   AS TERM_CODE,
  so.SUBJECT_ID                                  AS SUBJECT_ID,
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME                    AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID                  AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  so.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS                       AS NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
  so.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER                   AS SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER,
  ss.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY                          AS SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY,
  so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID                            AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  tip.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY                    AS TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
  tip.TERM_CODE                                   AS TIP_TERM_CODE,
  tip.SUBJECT_ID                                  AS TIP_SUBJECT_ID,
  tip.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME                    AS TIP_RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  tip.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID                  AS TIP_RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  tip.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS                       AS TIP_NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
  lib.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY                AS LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
  lib.TERM_CODE                                   AS LIBRARY_TERM_CODE,
  lib.SUBJECT_ID                                  AS LIBRARY_SUBJECT_ID,
  lib.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME                    AS LIBRARY_RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  lib.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID                  AS LIBRARY_RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  lib.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS                       AS LIBRARY_NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS
FROM subject_offered_core so
LEFT JOIN subject_summary_core ss
  ON ss.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
 AND ss.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN -- tip offerings: assume table name tip_subject_offered exists with required columns
  tip_subject_offered tip
  ON tip.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
 AND tip.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN -- library offerings: assume table name library_subject_offered exists with required columns
  library_subject_offered lib
  ON lib.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
 AND lib.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID
instructor_course_offerings.description: Wide, row-level listing of course/subject offerings and library/tip offerings with responsible faculty name and available enrollment counts. Each row is an offering or material-offering linkage exposing instructor fields and enrollment counts to allow matching by instructor name or MIT ID and later aggregation.

moira_members_with_sis_dept.name: moira_members_with_sis_dept
moira_members_with_sis_dept.body_sql:
SELECT
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME` AS `MOIRA_LIST_NAME`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` AS `MOIRA_LIST_KEY`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER` AS `MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` AS `MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID`,
  `sis_admin_department`.`SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS `SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  UPPER(`sis_admin_department`.`SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME`) AS `SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME`
FROM `moira_list_detail`
JOIN `moira_list`
  ON `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `sis_admin_department`
  ON (
       (`moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` IS NOT NULL
        AND `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` <> ''
        AND `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` = `sis_admin_department`.`SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE`)
       OR
       (`moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER` IS NOT NULL
        AND `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER` <> ''
        AND `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER` = `sis_admin_department`.`SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE`)
     )

rooms_canonicalized.name: rooms_canonicalized
rooms_canonicalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY AS FAC_ROOM_KEY,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fr.FLOOR AS FLOOR,
  fr.ROOM AS ROOM,
  COALESCE(fr.AREA, 0) AS AREA,
  fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS ORGANIZATION_NAME,
  frr.FCLT_ROOM_KEY AS FCLT_ROOM_KEY,
  frr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY AS FCLT_BUILDING_KEY,
  frr.FLOOR AS FLOOR_2,
  frr.ROOM AS ROOM_2,
  COALESCE(frr.AREA, 0) AS AREA_2,
  frr.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS ORGANIZATION_NAME_2
FROM fac_rooms fr
LEFT JOIN fclt_rooms frr
  ON (
       -- join by building and room identifiers when available
       (fr.BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL AND frr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL AND fr.BUILDING_KEY = frr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY)
       AND
       (fr.ROOM IS NOT NULL AND frr.ROOM IS NOT NULL AND fr.ROOM = frr.ROOM)
       AND
       (
         -- prefer matching floor when present, otherwise allow match on building+room alone
         (fr.FLOOR IS NOT NULL AND frr.FLOOR IS NOT NULL AND fr.FLOOR = frr.FLOOR)
         OR (fr.FLOOR IS NULL OR frr.FLOOR IS NULL)
       )
     )
rooms_canonicalized.description: Normalized canonical row per room combining both facility room tables into a consistent schema: one row per room with building key, floor, room id, area, organization and source provenance. Converts NULL area to zero and preserves original source to allow joining to the matching building table.

  fb.`DATE_BUILT` AS DATE_BUILT

LEFT JOIN buildings b
  ON fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER` IS NOT NULL
  AND b.`BUILDING_NUMBER` = fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`

fac_building_ownership_counts.name: fac_building_ownership_counts

fclt_rooms_per_building.name: fclt_rooms_per_building

fac_rooms_by_organization.name: fac_rooms_by_organization

fac_building_address_basic.name: fac_building_address_basic
fac_building_address_basic.description: One row per fac_building_address.BUILDING_KEY capturing building postal code and city for building-level reporting.

current_academic_terms.name: current_academic_terms

iap_detail_raw.name: iap_detail_raw
iap_detail_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY,
  iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY,
  iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY AS IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY,
  iap_subject_detail.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  -- cast ATTENDANCE to numeric; leave NULL if not numeric
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(iap_subject_detail.ATTENDANCE) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN iap_subject_detail.ATTENDANCE REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(iap_subject_detail.ATTENDANCE AS SIGNED)
    WHEN iap_subject_detail.ATTENDANCE REGEXP '^-?[0-9]*\\.[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(iap_subject_detail.ATTENDANCE AS DECIMAL(18,6))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS ATTENDANCE
FROM iap_subject_detail
iap_detail_raw.description: Row-level cohort of IAP subject detail rows (one row per iap_subject_detail record) exposing keys and raw fields needed for aggregation, joins to sessions and sponsors, and numeric-cast attendance.

iap_sponsor_key_name.name: iap_sponsor_key_name

  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` AS `LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`,
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` AS `LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY`
FROM `library_reserve_matrl_detail`
JOIN `library_reserve_catalog`
  ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = `library_reserve_catalog`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`
library_reserve_catalog_with_materials_j.description: Denormalized rows joining catalog entries to their reserved-material detail rows. One row per library_reserve_matrl_detail record with the catalog title included to simplify aggregation by course.

canonical_instructor_list.name: canonical_instructor_list
canonical_instructor_list.body_sql:
SELECT
  lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME AS INSTRUCTOR_NAME,
  lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY AS LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY,
  lso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  lso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID
FROM library_course_instructor lci
LEFT JOIN library_subject_offered lso
  ON lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME = lso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME
  -- Note: join made on exact instructor name equality to associate subject-offered responsible faculty rows.
canonical_instructor_list.description: Canonical list of instructors appearing in library instructor or subject-offered responsible faculty fields. One row per instructor name, exposing alternative id (MIT id when available) and canonical name column to use for exact-equality matching across tables.

library_reserve_catalog_rows_186.name: library_reserve_catalog_rows_186
library_reserve_catalog_rows_186.body_sql:
SELECT
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` AS `LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`,
  TRIM(`library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_YEAR`) AS `CATALOG_YEAR`,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_TITLE` AS `CATALOG_TITLE`,
  /* canonicalized title length: treat NULL title as length 0, else length of trimmed title */
  CASE
    WHEN `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_TITLE` IS NULL THEN 0
    ELSE CHAR_LENGTH(TRIM(`library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_TITLE`))
  END AS `CATALOG_TITLE_LENGTH`,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_AUTHOR_NAME` AS `CATALOG_AUTHOR_NAME`
FROM
  `library_reserve_catalog`

semantic_filters.library_reserve_catalog.CATALOG_YEAR: IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(CATALOG_YEAR) <> '' (logical filter; implement with SQL WHERE in final query if needed)

library_reserve_catalog_rows_186.description: One row per library reserve catalog entry (raw rows), with canonicalized publication year and title length. Treats NULL CATALOG_TITLE as length 0 and trims CATALOG_YEAR.

library_reserve_material_links.name: library_reserve_material_links
library_reserve_material_links.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- keys carried through from the detail row (grain)
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` AS `LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`,
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` AS `LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`,
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` AS `LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY`,
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` AS `LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`,

  -- attributes pulled from the referenced lookup / join tables
  `library_material_status`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS` AS `LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS`,
  `library_course_instructor`.`COURSE_NAME` AS `COURSE_NAME`,
  `library_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`
FROM
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`
  LEFT JOIN `library_material_status`
    ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = `library_material_status`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
  LEFT JOIN `library_course_instructor`
    ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` = `library_course_instructor`.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY`
  LEFT JOIN `library_subject_offered`
    ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` = `library_subject_offered`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
library_reserve_material_links.description: Denormalized links between reserve catalog entries and their material-detail and course/subject references. One row per library_reserve_matrl_detail linking a reserve catalog row to a material status, course_instructor, and library_subject_offered entry when available.

library_reserve_year_measures.name: library_reserve_year_measures
library_reserve_year_measures.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.CATALOG_YEAR AS CATALOG_YEAR,
  l.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY,
  l.CATALOG_TITLE AS CATALOG_TITLE,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY l.CATALOG_YEAR) AS TOTAL_CATALOG_ROWS_PER_YEAR,
  AVG(CHAR_LENGTH(COALESCE(l.CATALOG_TITLE, ''))) OVER (PARTITION BY l.CATALOG_YEAR) AS AVG_TITLE_LENGTH_PER_YEAR
FROM
  `library_reserve_catalog` l

semantic_filters.library_reserve_catalog.CATALOG_YEAR: IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(CATALOG_YEAR) <> '' (apply to include only non-empty years)

library_reserve_year_measures.description: Aggregated measures per publication year (one row per CATALOG_YEAR). Computes total number of catalog rows per year and average title length (treating NULL title as length 0). Does not compute distinct counts of statuses/courses from links; those are computed by joining with the link view to ensure only linked records are counted.
